Hi Ethan — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (pricing) and Rishi (contracts) to confirm exact contract language. Quick summary below that you can paste into the packet; Rishi will follow up with the formal definition we prefer in the MSA.

Short summary for procurement (paste-friendly):
- Billable unit: a "billable token" equals one input or output token as counted at the platform boundary. For streaming responses, tokens emitted during the stream are counted when generated; partial-byte rounding is to the nearest token unit.
- Rounding: tokens are counted per request (no per-request minimum). For streaming, we round per-chunk at the platform ingest boundary; in practice this is equivalent to rounding the total generated tokens per response.
- Commit & discounts: discounts are applied to billed token consumption after rounding. Monthly commits are aggregated by calendar month; unused committed tokens can be carried forward for a single month (true-up rules apply annually).

I'll let Rishi propose the legal wording around "billable units" and the exact rounding clause. Laura, any changes to the discount ladder behavior?

Marissa / Rishi — small pricing clarifications from my side before we hand to legal:

1) Discount ladder behavior — we apply volume discounts to the billed tokens after platform rounding. Example: 1,000,000 raw tokens -> rounded to 1,000,000 billed tokens -> discount from the tier that applies based on that billed amount.

2) Breakpoints: we define monthly breakpoints (e.g., 0-10M, 10M-50M, 50M+) and bucketed pricing; if a customer crosses a breakpoint mid-month we apply the higher tier to incremental usage only (marginal ladder, not retroactive above the first breakpoint).

3) Streaming: because streaming is token-emitted-first, we bill tokens when they land in the platform stream buffer. We do not charge per-stream session. That avoids per-session minimums your procurement asked about.

4) Commit terms: we offer monthly and annual commit constructs. For annual commits we pro-rate monthly buckets and allow quarterly true-ups. Any unused annual committed tokens roll to the next month only up to one month of carry-forward; excess are forfeited at year-end unless a true-up is executed.

If that aligns we can give procurement a short "billing appendix" snippet. I prefer to keep the legal clause tight: short definitions + examples and a reference to our metering appendix where we include precise rounding algorithm.

All — drafted a short contract-ready paragraph below. Please review and call out anything we shouldn't commit to. Once agreed I'll feed this into the SOW redlines.

----- PROPOSED CONTRACT LANGUAGE (metering & discounts) -----

"Billable Units". For purposes of invoicing, 'Billable Tokens' means the total number of input and output tokens processed by the Redwood Hosted API as measured at Redwood's platform boundary. Tokens are counted in whole units. For streaming responses, tokens shall be counted when generated by the model and emitted into Redwood's streaming buffer; Redwood's measurement at the platform boundary is determinative.

"Rounding". Token volumes will be measured and rounded to whole tokens at the time of measurement. No per-request minimum charge will apply. Rounding occurs at the platform ingestion boundary and is applied before any discount calculations.

"Discount Application". Volume discounts set forth in the Order apply to the billed token quantity after rounding. Volume breakpoints are applied on a marginal basis within each calendar month (i.e., incremental usage at higher breakpoints is billed at the corresponding breakpoint price; previously billed usage is not re-priced retroactively into higher breakpoints).

"Commits and True-ups". Monthly committed token volumes are aggregated per calendar month. Unused committed tokens may be carried forward to the immediate subsequent month up to a cap equal to one month of the committed quantity. Annual commitments will be pro-rated and may be subject to quarterly true-ups as set forth in the Order.

----- end proposed language -----

If everyone signs off I will drop this into proposed_metering_redlines.docx and share with Helio's procurement. Note: I intentionally left algorithmic-level details (e.g., chunking window size) out of the MSA and put them into the metering appendix. Any objections?

Thanks,

Ethan — quick answers and a sample table (I attached SOW_v2.pdf with a 3-line example on page 2):

- Streaming rounding example: We round to whole tokens per response at measurement time. Example: a response that emits 1,234.6 raw tokens will be billed as 1,235 billed tokens. If a single user opens multiple streaming connections for the same logical request, each emitted stream is measured independently; in practice customers see billed tokens ~= sum of emitted tokens.

- Marginal ladder: discounts apply within the calendar month on billed tokens only (confirmed). We will provide daily-granularity usage exports in the Console and a CSV export in the billing portal for reconciliation.

- Appendix/example: see attached SOW_v2.pdf (page 2) which shows: Raw tokens -> Billed tokens (after rounding) -> Price applied at each breakpoint -> Total charge. We'll also push a short one-page PDF to the shared Drive if procurement wants a standalone handout.
